Abul Kalam Moinuddin, Advocate, instructed by Chowdhury Md. Zahangir Advocate-on-Record.   ------ For the Petitioners.

Faruqur Rahman. ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Joint District Judge and Additional Artha Rin Adalat No.2, Dhaka and Others. ------ Respondents.
full_judgment:
2. Facts, as placed before the High Court Division, in short, are that the respondent No.2, the National Bank Limited, as plaintiff, filed Money Suit No, 19 of 1992 in the Artha Rin Adalat No.2, Dhaka against the writ petitioner and the respondent Nos.3118 for recovery of loan money amounting to TK.75, 77,481.48. The suit was ultimately decreed ex-parte on 30.06.1999. Thereafter, on the basis of that decree, the decree holder bank started Artha Jari Execution Case No.28 of 2002 against the judgment debtors including the present writ petitioner for realization of decreetal amount. Since, the judgment debtors did not pay the decrectal amount, the decree holder bank prayed for issuance of warrant of arrest against the judgment debtors and by the impugned order the learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat issued warrant of arrest against the judgment debtors including the writ petitioner. 

 4. Mr. Abul Kalam Moinuddin, the Teamed Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that the petitioner has paid TK. 5,10,000/- against the loan liability complying with the direction of the High Court Division which is thrice of the principal loan amount; in view of above facts, the judgment and order of the High Court Division is liable to interfered with. He further submits that the High Court Division has erred in law in not considering that the plaint of the Money Suit is not made in accordance with the provision provided under Order 7, Rule 2& 7 of the Code of Civil procedure; that is why the same cannot be sustained in the eye of law and hence the decree drawn in the suit is barred and as such the judgment and order of the High Court Division is liable to be interfered. He further submits that the High Court Division has erred in law without considering that it appears from the plaint that admittedly the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 took loan of TK. 1,70,000/- but the respondent No.2 claimed TK. 75,77,481.48 for recovery and asked for decree which is an imaginary amount and there is no explanation how TK. 1,70,000/- increased to TK. 75,77,481.48 and how the said loan was guaranteed and what are the charge and documents made against the said loan; not only that there is no schedule of the property which was made charge against the aforesaid loan and as such the judgment and order of the High Court Division is liable to be interfered. He lastly submits that the High Court Division has erred in law not considering that the joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat (respondent No.1) drew a decree at TK. 75,77,481.48 though admittedly the loan sanction was only 1,70,000/- which is barred under provision of section 47 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and as such the judgment and order of the High Court Division is liable to be interfered with. 

 6. The learned Judges of the High Court Division came to clear finding that admittedly this writ petitioner is one of the judgment debtors and as such he is also responsible for payment of the decreetal amount and the warrant of arrest has been issued against all other judgment debtors also under Section 34(1) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 for the purpose of making them compelled to pay the decreetal amount and held that no illegality has been committed in passing the impugned order issuing warrant of arrest against the judgment debtors including the writ petitioner and discharged the Rule accordingly directing the petitioner to surrender before the Execution Court concerned within 60 days from the date of order and further directing the police not to arrest him within 60 days in connection with the Artha Jari Case in question.
